task: Prevent self-host story worktrees from silently executing a stale global Lattice runtime.
outcome: A bare global lattice command launched inside a Proofbound story worktree exits before handler dispatch with reasonCode=stale_global_runtime_in_worktree and prints exactly one recovery command: node bin/lattice.js <same command>; the local entrypoint then succeeds.
facts: B-914f spent 7 minutes 28 seconds under the main-workspace global runtime instead of the worktree build.
bin/bootstrap-runner.js already fails clearly when local dist artifacts are missing and marks global fallback heartbeat-only.
runtime-fact-registry.ts and runtime-environment-checks.ts already model cli entrypoint, global core realpath, self versus external scope, and doctor output.
runCli resolves normalized command, root and active story before handler registry dispatch, providing a pre-mutation enforcement seam.
resolveActiveCliEntrypoint already canonicalizes process.argv[1] through safeRealpath-aware classification, so a separate bootstrap marker is not required for symlinked launchers.

The only worktree exemption needed is an explicitly marked LATTICE_CODEX_ENTRYPOINT=global-fallback session_brief heartbeat; help/version return before dispatch, and post-merge main checks are not worktree mismatches.
constraints: External consumer repositories must continue to use a global installation without a hard self-host mismatch gate.
Read-only global fallback may remain usable only for explicitly marked session_brief heartbeat in a self-host story worktree.
Detection must occur before expensive validation or story-scoped mutation and expose a stable reason code.
Runtime facts stay in runtime-fact-registry and its contract verifier; process facts are not expanded.
